title: Lower bound for decoding an edge
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with $q>0$, let $F$ be a table of real-valued functions on the Boolean cube, let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$, and choose a default alphabet coordinate, a vertex $v$, a neighbour $w$ of $v$, and a coordinate $i$. If $i$ is influential for the averaged neighbour function at $v$ according to the $\varepsilon$ threshold, and the inverse image of $i$ under the constraint permutation is influential for the function at $w$ according to the $\varepsilon/2$ threshold, then the ordinary candidate-decoding edge value is at least $1/(4q^2)$.
